`kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer` creates an `AWSPCAClusterIssuer` custom resource, but that CRD (`awspca.cert-manager.io`) is only registered by the `aws-privateca-issuer` add-on installed by `module.eks_blueprints_kubernetes_addons` (enable_aws_privateca_issuer = true). Nothing orders this manifest after the add-ons module, so applying it before the CRD exists will fail. (Contrast with `kubectl_manifest.example_pca_certificate`, which does depends_on the add-ons module.) No clean data reference exists to the add-ons module, so a bare `depends_on` on it is the appropriate fix.

`kubectl_manifest.cluster_pca_issuer` registers an `AWSPCAClusterIssuer` pointing at `aws_acmpca_certificate_authority.example`, but an ACM PCA root CA cannot issue certificates until it is activated by associating its own certificate — which `aws_acmpca_certificate_authority_certificate.example` does. Nothing depends on that activation resource (it is a leaf), so the issuer can be created against a still-PENDING_CERTIFICATE CA. This operational readiness ordering isn't expressed by any attribute reference or depends_on.

`aws_eks_node_group.managed_ng` references `aws_iam_role.managed_ng[0].arn` via `node_role_arn`, which already establishes the implicit dependency. Listing `aws_iam_role.managed_ng` again in the resource's `depends_on` duplicates that ordering and is redundant (the other two depends_on entries — instance profile and policy attachment — are not implicit and should stay).
